assumptions.name: beta
assumptions.justification: Microsoft's published five-year monthly beta sits near 0.9. Used only when the platform's own regression proposes nothing, and recorded as a finding when it is.

assumptions.name: capex_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of capital expenditure over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.1205, 0.1326, 0.1814, 0.2291, 0.3494.

assumptions.name: depreciation_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of depreciation and amortisation over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.0736, 0.0637, 0.0816, 0.0994, 0.1175.

assumptions.name: ebit_margin
assumptions.justification: The mean of operating income over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.4206, 0.4177, 0.4464, 0.4562, 0.4678.

assumptions.name: equity_risk_premium
assumptions.justification: 4.5 %: inside the 4-6 % band the operator's audit policy accepts, and the neighbourhood of the implied US premium in the Damodaran monthly series through 2026. A judgement, stated as one.

assumptions.name: exit_multiple
assumptions.justification: Anchored on two things pulling opposite ways. Upward: EBIT margin 0.4418 and rising (0.4678 in FY2026), plus D&A of 0.0872 of revenue, describe an unusually high-margin franchise that has historically traded at a premium EV/EBITDA to the market. Downward: capex intensity has trebled to 0.3494 in FY2026 against a 0.2026 mean, and finance lease interest roughly doubled FY2025-FY2026 — EBITDA is becoming a much poorer proxy for cash at Microsoft, and a 0.05 risk-free rate is far above the regime in which MSFT's historical high-teens/low-20s multiples were set. 13x is below those historical levels for that reason, and I flag that any exit multiple is market-convention-anchored rather than filing-derived. Consistency: paired with 0.03 growth and the capex intensity above, I regard the perpetuity-growth terminal value as the better estimate; this multiple is the cross-check, and it would need to rise toward 16-18x only if you believe capex reverts toward the 0.2026 mean. If FY2027 capex stays near 0.35, 10-11x is the more defensible figure.

assumptions.name: revenue_growth
assumptions.justification: The compound annual growth rate of revenue from 2022-06-30 to 2026-06-30, over 4 year(s): revenue moved from 198,270,000,000 to 331,839,000,000. Held flat across the forecast, because a trailing rate is one number and projecting a fade is a judgement this derivation does not make.

assumptions.name: risk_free_rate
assumptions.justification: The US 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield was 5% on 2026-09-15, as published by 2026-09-17 (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), series DGS10). Taken as the USD risk-free rate for this run's as-of date and converted to the fraction 0.05.

assumptions.name: tax_rate
assumptions.justification: The mean of income tax expense over pre tax income across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.1311, 0.1898, 0.1823, 0.1763, 0.1940.

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.justification: Taken to sit below any ordinary cost of capital here: with the derived risk-free rate at 0.05, an equity-financed megacap WACC would plausibly land near 0.085-0.095, so 0.03 leaves ample spread and stays inside the platform's 0.04 cap. Grounding: a dominant software/cloud franchise in a still-expanding category should hold pricing and volume roughly with long-run nominal GDP forever, but not above it — the 0.1374 trailing revenue CAGR and the AI/'Agents and Infra' concentration are cyclical drivers, not perpetual ones. The 5% risk-free suggests a higher nominal-growth regime, which argues against 0.02. Lower it toward 0.02-0.025 if the confirmed discount rate falls below ~0.07, or if you judge cloud/AI pricing to deflate in the terminal year.

assumptions.name: working_capital_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of net working capital — current assets less current liabilities — over revenue, across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. A negative figure is normal for a business paid before it pays, and is proposed as it stands rather than floored at zero.
